Quick wins you can do today
- Enable Low Power Mode when you’re out and about; turn it off when you don’t need it.
- Screen first: use Auto-Brightness, reduce brightness a notch, and shorten Auto‑Lock.
- Tame background drain: set Background App Refresh to Wi‑Fi only or off for nonessential apps; set Location Services to “While Using.”
- Manage notifications you mirror to your Apple Watch—fewer buzzes = fewer screen wake-ups on your phone.
- Poor signal = big drain while traveling. In low-signal areas, switch to LTE (instead of 5G Auto) or use Airplane Mode plus Wi‑Fi.

Use your existing gear more efficiently

- If your phone has a thick case, remove it when wirelessly charging to reduce heat and improve efficiency.
- Keep a short, high‑quality USB‑C/USB‑A to Lightning/USB‑C cable in your tech pouch for fast PD charging on the go.

Apple Watch-specific tweaks
- Let the Watch handle quick glances (timers, notifications, directions) so you don’t wake your phone screen as often.
- Trim mirrored notifications on the Watch to only what you need (Messages, calendar), reducing double wake-ups.
- If you have a cellular Watch, keep cellular off unless you truly need it; it can increase overall device power use.

- Download offline maps/playlists on Wi‑Fi before flights/train rides.
- In transit, use Airplane Mode if you’re between towers (e.g., subways, rural stretches).
- Avoid charging the phone and power bank stacked together in your pouch; trapped heat is bad for both batteries.

- iPhone: Settings > Battery > Battery Health & Charging. If Maximum Capacity < 80% or you see repeated unexpected shutdowns, a battery service will make a noticeable difference.
- Battery usage charts: identify any app spiking background activity; restrict its background refresh or location.
- If standby drain is high, try Reset Network Settings and unpair old Bluetooth accessories.

- Use a 20W+ PD wall charger for faster, cooler top‑ups at the hotel.
- Aim for partial charges (20–80%) day‑to‑day; avoid leaving the phone hot on a charger for hours.
